facts.text: I am creating a Vehicle Owner and User Management service for Polestar.
The Vehicle Owner and User Management service has four modules: the Registration number, owner, primary driver, and market modules.
I will focus on the Primary Driver module.
The Primary Driver module tracks the user identified with a Polestar ID who is the primary driver of a car.
A car can only have one primary driver.
The primary driver is captured from Polestar's Order Management System (POMS).
The service listens to order events from POMS.
If an order event contains a valid VIN and a Polestar ID in the "Driver" field, the service saves that Polestar ID as the car's primary driver.
A Polestar ID is valid if it exists in the Polestar ID service, which can be confirmed with an API call.
A VIN is valid if it exists in Volvo's factory order system, the Vehicle Internet Sale & Traceability Application (VISTA).
The service stores all the events it receives in an "event store" for replay purposes.
The service allows other systems to change a car's primary driver through an API.
There are two versions of the API: one with M2M authentication and one with Polestar ID authentication (OAuth).
Using the Polestar ID Auth. version, the user can only edit a car's primary driver if they have access to the logged-in primary driver's credentials.
The service saves the system that made the update for primary driver changes.
The service saves the timestamp of when the primary driver was registered.
The service saves the user ID if the change was made using the Polestar ID auth API.
The service saves the client ID of the service that made the change if the change was made using M2M auth API.
The service saves the event ID that caused the change.
If the update was made based on an event, the service also saves the timestamp when the event was emitted.
If the primary driver is registered based on an event from POMS, the service stores the order ID from the event.
A POMS update can only overwrite an API update if the order ID is new.
The service maintains a history for primary drivers.
When a new primary driver is registered, the previous primary driver is given an end timestamp.
Using the APIs, it is possible to remove a primary driver from a car without registering a new one.
I asked to create a data model in DynamoDB for the primary driver module.
The service will save the name of the system that initiated the change.
If the change was made based on an event, the service will save the name of the system that emitted the event.
If the change was made through the API, the service will save the name of the system that made the request.
I asked for all attributes in a list with descriptions.
System and SystemName shall be the same attribute.
